episodePairs.scene: Two adults meet at a neighborhood language exchange; one points gently to themself.
episodePairs.pictureBrief: Two adults meeting, one hand lightly on their own chest, calm friendly eye contact; no written words or speech bubbles.
episodePairs.pictureAlt: At a language exchange, one adult touches his chest as he tells another person his name.

en.prompt: 처음 만난 사람에게 자기 이름을 말해 보세요. 알렉스 대신 내 이름을 넣어요.
en.pronunciation: I'm sounds like one short beat; say your name clearly.

ko.title: Say Your Name
ko.prompt: You meet someone new. Say your own name instead of Alex.
ko.pronunciation: 저는 / 알렉스예요; listen to how the name joins 예요.
ko.register: polite everyday self-introduction to an unfamiliar adult

episodePairs.metaTransfer: Replace only the name; keep a natural introduction.

episodePairs.scene: A café worker hands the learner a cup of water.
episodePairs.pictureBrief: A server gently handing a glass of water to an adult customer; both visible; no text.
episodePairs.pictureAlt: A café worker gives a customer a glass of water and he smiles in thanks.

en.pronunciation: TH sounds with the tongue near the teeth; keep both words connected.

ko.title: Say Thank You
ko.prompt: A café worker gives you a glass of water. Thank them.
ko.pronunciation: 감사합니다 (gamsahamnida); listen for the natural flow of 합니다.
ko.register: polite thanks to an unfamiliar adult

episodePairs.metaTransfer: Use the same phrase when a stranger helps in a different place.

episodePairs.scene: At a small café counter, the learner needs to call a staff member who is nearby.
episodePairs.pictureBrief: An adult customer raising a small open hand at a café counter toward a nearby staff member; no text.
episodePairs.pictureAlt: A customer raises his hand to get a café worker's attention.

en.prompt: 카페 직원에게 말을 걸고 싶어요. 먼저 어떻게 부를까요?
en.pronunciation: ex-CUSE me; the middle part is stressed.

ko.title: Get Attention
ko.prompt: You want to get a café worker's attention. What do you say?
ko.pronunciation: 저기요 (jeogiyo); keep the ending gentle rather than shouting.
ko.register: everyday call for service, not an apology

episodePairs.metaTransfer: Use an attention-getter before making a request.

episodePairs.scene: A staff member offers another drink, and the learner already has enough.
episodePairs.pictureBrief: An adult customer smiling and gently shaking their head as a server offers another drink; no text.
episodePairs.pictureAlt: A customer gently raises his hand to decline another drink from a server.

en.prompt: 직원이 음료를 더 주겠다고 해요. 필요 없을 때 정중하게 답해 보세요.
en.pronunciation: Pause lightly after No; keep thank you warm.

ko.title: Decline Politely
ko.prompt: Someone offers you another drink, but you don't need one. Reply politely.
ko.pronunciation: 아니요 / 괜찮아요; listen for the connected sound in 괜찮아요.
ko.register: polite everyday decline to an unfamiliar adult

episodePairs.metaTransfer: Decline without sounding angry or abrupt.

episodePairs.scene: The learner sits at a café table and needs drinking water.
episodePairs.pictureBrief: An adult customer at a café table indicating an empty water glass while talking to a server; no text.
episodePairs.pictureAlt: A customer points to an empty glass while asking a café worker for water.

en.target: Can I have some water, please?
en.prompt: 빈 물잔이 있어요. 직원에게 물을 부탁해 보세요.
en.expected: Can I have some water, please?
en.pronunciation: Can I links together; keep the request gentle.

ko.title: Ask for Water
ko.meaning: Could I have some water, please?
ko.prompt: Your glass is empty. Ask a café worker for water.
ko.pronunciation: 물 좀 / 주세요; say the whole request smoothly.
ko.register: polite everyday request to café staff

episodePairs.metaTransfer: Ask for a needed object without adding a grammar explanation first.

episodePairs.scene: At a station desk, a staff member speaks and the learner cannot hear clearly.
episodePairs.pictureBrief: An adult learner leaning slightly toward a station information clerk, one hand gently cupped near an ear; no text.
episodePairs.pictureAlt: A traveler cups his hand near his ear and asks a station clerk to repeat herself.

en.prompt: 안내 방송을 잘 못 들었어요. 직원에게 다시 말해 달라고 해 보세요.
en.pronunciation: ONE more TIME, please; keep please light.

ko.title: Ask to Hear It Again
ko.prompt: You missed what the station clerk said. Ask them to repeat it.
ko.pronunciation: 다시 / 말씀해 주세요; listen to the polite request ending.
ko.register: polite request to an unfamiliar adult

episodePairs.metaTransfer: Use the same repair move when you miss any important spoken instruction.

episodePairs.scene: The learner is inside a station and cannot find the restroom.
episodePairs.pictureBrief: An adult traveler looking around a station lobby for a restroom, then speaking to an information clerk; a simple restroom symbol may be visible, no words.
episodePairs.pictureAlt: A traveler asks a station clerk for the restroom, which is marked by a pictogram nearby.

en.prompt: 역에서 화장실을 찾고 있어요. 직원에게 물어보세요.
en.pronunciation: Where's joins where + is; keep restroom clear.

ko.title: Find the Restroom
ko.prompt: You cannot find the restroom at a station. Ask a staff member.
ko.pronunciation: 화장실이 / 어디예요; keep the question ending gentle.
ko.register: polite everyday question to an unfamiliar adult

episodePairs.metaTransfer: Ask for the location of another needed place.

episodePairs.scene: A traveler cannot lift a heavy suitcase onto a low train rack.
episodePairs.pictureBrief: An adult traveler struggling safely with a heavy suitcase beside a train luggage rack and looking to a nearby adult for help; no text.
episodePairs.pictureAlt: A traveler asks another adult for help lifting a heavy suitcase on a train.

en.prompt: 무거운 가방을 혼자 들기 어려워요. 옆 사람에게 도움을 청해 보세요.
en.pronunciation: Please HELP me; keep the final word clear.

ko.title: Ask for Help
ko.prompt: Your suitcase is too heavy to lift alone. Ask a nearby person for help.
ko.pronunciation: 저 좀 / 도와주세요; keep the request polite and direct.
ko.register: polite request to an unfamiliar adult

episodePairs.metaTransfer: Use the phrase when you need help with a different physical task.

episodePairs.scene: The learner leaves a small shop while the clerk remains inside.
episodePairs.pictureBrief: An adult customer at a shop door waving goodbye to a clerk who stays behind the counter; no text.
episodePairs.pictureAlt: A customer waves goodbye as he leaves a shop while the clerk remains inside.

en.prompt: 가게에서 나오며 직원에게 작별 인사를 해 보세요.
en.pronunciation: good-BYE; let the second part rise and fall naturally.

ko.title: Say Goodbye When Leaving
ko.prompt: You leave a shop while the clerk stays inside. What do you say?
ko.pronunciation: 안녕히 / 계세요; use this form when you are the one leaving.
ko.register: polite leave-taking to an adult who remains

episodePairs.metaTransfer: Choose the leave-taking form by noticing who stays and who goes.
